findings.summary: The architecture shows persistence going through the bus, but pages 5 and 6 persist synchronously before the ack, so the write path contradicts itself.
findings.evidence: Page 3 flow: "chat -> bus -> store". Page 5: "persist before any ack" with "cs -> db: 1 tick ack". Page 6: "svc -> own (seq) -> cas (quorum)", with no Kafka.
findings.fix: State on page 3 that the chat service assigns seq and writes to Cassandra synchronously, then acks, and that Kafka carries only the async consumers (fan-out, push). Redraw the page 3 diagram to match.

findings.summary: The `seq` and `sync{since_seq}` frame are used before `seq` is defined or explained.
findings.evidence: "C>S sync{since_seq}" and "Then `sync{since_seq}` fetches missed" appear here, but the per-chat `seq` is first introduced on page 5 and explained on page 6 ("seq beats clocks!").
findings.fix: Add a one-line definition on page 4 ("seq = per-chat increasing counter assigned by the server on persist; see Storage"), or move the sync frame and failure recovery to after the ordering page.

findings.summary: The seq owner and its per-chat counter are asserted without any mechanism or example of how a single owner is chosen or survives failure.
findings.evidence: "Per-chat seq | partition counter +1 | Yes" and the "Seq owner" node with no explanation. Page 14 repeats "per-chat `seq`, one owner".
findings.fix: Add a short example: chat_id hashes to one owner node, which increments a counter (for example 980 -> 981) and writes. Say what happens when the owner dies (a new owner is elected and resumes from max(seq)).

findings.summary: Describes uploading 5 MB chunks to a single presigned PUT URL, which S3 does not support; chunking needs multipart upload with a presigned URL per part.
findings.evidence: "POST /media/upload-url -> {url, media_id}", "PUT {url}   # 5 MB chunks", and edge "2 presigned PUT"
findings.fix: Have the API return a multipart upload ID plus presigned UploadPart URLs (parts of at least 5 MiB, except the last). Use a single presigned PUT only for small files, and have /complete call CompleteMultipartUpload.

findings.summary: Claims at-least-once delivery plus dedupe gives exactly-once, which overstates the guarantee.
findings.fix: Write "effectively-once (idempotent processing)". Exactly-once delivery is not achievable over an unreliable network; dedupe only makes the processing effect happen once.
